name: final_tiebreak_decision

oracle.source: .kiro/specs/ascension-trials-scalable-two-player-analysis (VS3 Task 9; REQ-7.3 final Spellbook tiebreak; REQ-4/REQ-5/REQ-6). Best-response values hand-derived from the final-result rules of configs/toy/final_tiebreak_decision.json (model v2.1 §8.2 spell_count; spec v1.1 §7.9).

provenance: VS3 best-response planted fixture BR-FINALTIE-1 (REQ-9.4 provenance discipline: every expected value below is derived by hand from the rules, not reverse-engineered from oracle output). Config configs/toy/final_tiebreak_decision.json: one fungible domain; Trials t1, t2 each reward first=2 (second=0); shared-full ties; local total_power tiebreak; optional allocation; the FINAL chain is [spell_count, shared]. When Recognition-Point totals are equal, sole first place is decided by the derived-state spell_count statistic. Acting side A holds fungible=1 with spell_count=5; fixed opponent B holds fungible=1 with spell_count=1 and plays its unit on t1. With one unit A can only reach a 2-2 Recognition-Point tie (contest t1 for a shared 2-2, or take the uncontested t2 while B takes t1, again 2-2). On that 2-2 tie the final chain compares spell_count: A(5) > B(1), so A takes SOLE first and wins the game -- an outcome produced entirely by the final Spellbook tiebreak, never by Recognition Points. Hand-derivation: the row win best response is +1 (decided at the final spell_count tiebreak on a 2-2 RP tie); the row margin best response is 0 (A cannot out-score B on Recognition Points with equal budget and shared-full ties, so the best margin is a 2-2 tie -> 0). Because an active final Spellbook tiebreak couples the decision across Trials, the margin oracle takes the exact exhaustive path (REQ-4.3, evidence class exact_exhaustive_best_response) while the win oracle models the RP-tie -> A-wins sign directly (numerical_milp_best_response_certified).

expected.opponent_description: B plays its single unit on t1
